races.name: Texel Trail
races.notes: Beach and dune trails: sand slows everyone down, so judge pace on the firm parts and run by effort in soft sand. Stretch goal, no stress: a strong finish beats a fast start. The volleyball match on Friday 5 Feb: play light, early to bed.

races.name: Beer Lovers Marathon
races.goal: Finish comfortably, together with the mates
races.notes: No time goal: run at easy-long-run effort and enjoy the tastings in moderation (water first!). Saturday at Nerdland: comfortable shoes, limit time on your feet, carb-rich dinner, early night.

races.name: Iron Viking
races.notes: A marathon with obstacles: expect 6-8 hours. Pace by effort, eat every 45 min, keep your grip fresh by not over-gripping on the run sections. Trail shoes with good drainage, gloves optional.

phases.name: 10k race week
phases.about: Training volume drops, one short session at race pace on Thursday keeps the legs sharp, and Saturday is a shake-out.

phases.name: Reset
phases.about: Easy running only. The 10k result is entered as new fitness and the Texel block is paced from it.

phases.name: Texel build
phases.focus: Long runs to 22 km, threshold, hills and dunes.
phases.about:
Twelve weeks that grow the long run from 12 to 22 km while adding one quality session a week.
Every fourth week is lighter so the body can absorb the work (and those weeks line up with your birthday and Christmas).
From January a fourth run and a strength session come in, because volleyball takes less of the week.
Specific work for Texel: dune long runs, hill repeats and race-pace blocks on sand.

phases.name: Texel taper
phases.about: Volume down by half, a little race pace on Wednesday, nothing on Thursday and Friday except the match.

phases.name: Marathon build
phases.focus: Long runs to 32 km, durability and fuelling.
phases.about:
After a recovery week, the long run grows from 16 to 32 km (peak on 19 April).
With no time goal, the quality work is about durability: tempo, hills and steady runs rather than marathon-pace sessions.
The wintersport week is a step-back week; Easter Monday hosts a big long run. Practise eating and drinking on every long run over 90 minutes.

phases.name: Marathon week
phases.focus: Rest, Nerdland, then 42 km with the mates.
phases.about: Short and easy. Saturday at the festival counts as rest day: sit when you can.

phases.name: Recovery & holiday
phases.about: Three weeks without structure: easy runs when you feel like it, hikes, swims. This is where a marathon is absorbed.

phases.name: Iron Viking build
phases.focus: Trail long runs to 33 km, strength, grip and obstacles.
phases.about:
Fifteen weeks to turn a marathon runner into an obstacle-course runner.
Long runs move to trails and grow to 33 km; Saturdays alternate trail runs with OCR circuits (run, burpees, hangs, carries).
Two strength sessions a week (Tuesday and Thursday) build the grip and upper body that obstacles demand.
Every fourth week is lighter.

phases.name: Iron Viking week
phases.about: Easy running, no strength work after Tuesday.

journal.title: The plan starts
journal.body:
Four races in eleven months: a 10k benchmark, Texel Trail (24 km), the Beer Lovers Marathon and Iron Viking (42 km with obstacles).

Starting point from the watch data: about two runs a week since late July, longest run 16.6 km, easy pace around 6:30-7:00/km.
The main point to work on: most runs were at heart-rate zone 3-4, which means "easy" days weren't easy.
The last two runs (21 and 25 October) were mostly in zone 2, which is exactly right. Keep doing that.

Fitness is estimated at VDOT 38 (predicts 52:15 for 10k). Sunday's 10k replaces that estimate and re-paces the Texel block.

journal.title: Knee niggle, almost gone
journal.body:
Some knee trouble in the week of 19 October; by today it is almost gone.
Today's easy run with strides became 30 min on the elliptical.

journal.title: Easier race week, and the elliptical joins the plan
journal.body:
This week is two easy runs (Thursday 5 km, Saturday shake-out) instead of a race-pace session, so the knee arrives at Sunday's 10k calm. If it hurts during the warm-up, run the 10k as an easy training run: no result is worth weeks off.

The elliptical and kettlebells at home are a real asset:
- Every easy and recovery run now shows an elliptical alternative (same heart-rate zone, about the same time). Use it whenever the knee or legs feel beaten up, or when the weather is grim.
- Long runs, quality sessions and the race-specific trail runs stay running: bones, tendons and feet only get race-ready from the impact of running, and Texel, the marathon and Iron Viking are all long days on your feet.
- The strength sessions are now a kettlebell circuit (goblet squats, swings, single-leg deadlifts, carries). Strong hips and thighs are the best protection for knees.
- Day after the 10k is an elliptical session instead of a recovery run.
